spec.goal: Extend GET /health on the toy items API so its 200 JSON body carries an integer uptime_seconds (>= 0) derived from the Node process start time, alongside the existing unchanged status: "ok" field, so operators can see how long the process has been up. Implementation lives in the /health handler in toy/src/app.js using process.uptime() floored to a whole number; the existing health test is updated to assert the new shape.

acceptance.given: a running toy app created by createApp() from toy/src/app.js
acceptance.then: the response status is 200, the Content-Type is JSON, and the parsed body has exactly the keys status and uptime_seconds (no other keys)
body.status strictly equals the string "ok" (unchanged from current behavior)
body.uptime_seconds is of type number, satisfies Number.isInteger(body.uptime_seconds) === true, and is >= 0

acceptance.given: a running toy app and a captured baseline b = Math.floor(process.uptime()) taken in the test process immediately before the request
acceptance.then: body.uptime_seconds >= b and body.uptime_seconds <= Math.floor(process.uptime()) + 1 measured immediately after the response, proving the value tracks process start rather than being a constant or a wall-clock epoch

acceptance.given: a running toy app that has already served one GET /health returning uptime_seconds = u1
acceptance.when: the test waits at least 1100 ms and sends a second GET /health returning u2
acceptance.then: u2 > u1 and u2 - u1 >= 1, showing the value increases with elapsed process time

acceptance.given: two separate app instances created by two calls to createApp() within the same test process (as test/helpers.js start() does per test)
acceptance.when: GET /health is called on each instance
acceptance.then: both return integer uptime_seconds values derived from the same process start (they differ by at most 1), i.e. uptime is not reset per app instance

acceptance.given: the toy package as checked out
acceptance.when: the suite is run via `npm test` in toy/ (node --test "test/*.test.js")
acceptance.then: all tests pass, including toy/test/items.test.js unchanged — GET /items, POST /items success (201) and POST /items missing/invalid name (400 { error: "name is required" }) behave exactly as before

touched_surfaces.ref: GET /health (200 response body: adds uptime_seconds integer field; status field unchanged)

out_of_scope: Any change to GET /items, POST /items, or the in-memory item store and its validation rules (wi-1 and wi-2 remain untouched by this work item).
Adding further health/diagnostic fields such as version, hostname, pid, memory, timestamp, started_at, or dependency checks.
New routes (e.g. /healthz, /ready, /live, /metrics) or changing the /health path, method, or HTTP status codes.
Sub-second precision, floating-point, string/ISO-duration, or millisecond-based uptime representations — the field is a floored integer number of seconds.
Per-app-instance or per-request uptime tracking (e.g. recording Date.now() inside createApp()) as the source of truth; the value must come from process start.
Changes to toy/src/server.js, toy/package.json, dependencies, or the shared test harness in toy/test/helpers.js.
Authentication, rate limiting, caching headers, or observability/monitoring integrations for /health.
Updating toy/README.md route documentation (optional, not gating).
Any files outside the toy/ directory, including toy/backlog.json.
risk_reasons: Backward-compatible additive change only; existing status field unchanged
No data schema, auth, payments, or infrastructure changes
Isolated to a single diagnostic endpoint with no impact on core items API
Fully reversible with no permanent side effects or migrations
Well-scoped with clear acceptance criteria and comprehensive test coverage

tasks.description: Extend GET /health response in toy/src/app.js to include an uptime_seconds integer field derived from Math.floor(process.uptime()). The /health handler should return both the existing status: 'ok' field and the new uptime_seconds field, meeting all acceptance criteria.

owned_surfaces.ref: GET /health (200 response body: adds uptime_seconds integer field; status field unchanged)
